title: Three Nights and One Short Helmet
subtitle: 火灾安全 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 火灾安全（灾害防范·火灾与安全）
meta: 主题语境：火灾安全（灾害防范·火灾与安全）　|　核心词汇：fireman　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fireman 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the captain ① thanked a fireman that no officer in the station would have named, and he said the thanking was the whole of the night. The ② fireman, meaning the man himself and not the engine, ran three nights and stayed unnamed in the book; a fireman, he said, is the only thing in a station that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ fireman in that station had the same short helmet beside him, and the ④ fireman at the far door, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A fireman, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; the captain said the naming is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the fireman was the whole of the matter, meaning the stoker and not the man. The ⑥ fireman, meaning the stoker and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody names; fireman, he said, is either somebody you thank or the only word that means both a firefighter and a stoker. He said the stoker is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ fireman had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short helmet. The ⑧ fireman of the whole thing, the captain wrote in February, was one station and three nights of naming; fireman, he said, is either the one at the far door or the reason you learned to name. He said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ fireman I remember is the one named in the plan, which closed in 1972 and is still described as the quietest in the station. A ⑩ fireman, my mother said in 1974, is the only one that improves by being named; every fireman, she said, is a stoker that has agreed to look like a firefighter. She said the stoker was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 消防员（指消防站里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 消防员（指那一位本身，与消防车相对）
C. 固定搭配：thank a fireman 感谢一位消防员
D. n. 消防员（指留给孩子们的那一位）
E. n. 消防员（抽象总称，指一座消防站的称谢之事）
F. n. 消防员（指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一位）
G. n. 司炉工；烧火工（指一件事里人人都等却无人说出名字的那样人）
H. n. 司炉工（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说出名字的那样人）

items.q: thanked a fireman that no officer in the station would have named
The fireman, meaning the man himself and not the engine
the fireman at the far door
the fireman was the whole of the matter
the fireman had become a line in a plan
The fireman of the whole thing
A fireman, my mother said in 1974

answers.why: thank a fireman 意为“感谢一位消防员”，1963 年队长感谢了一位消防站里没有一位长官肯说出名字的消防员。
fireman 意为“消防员”，指那一位本身而不是消防车，他经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被说出名字。
fireman 意为“消防员”，指消防站里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一顶矮矮的头盔。
fireman 意为“消防员”，指留给孩子们的那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
fireman 意为“司炉工、烧火工”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说出名字的那样人，叔叔说那位司炉工就是那件事的全部。
fireman 意为“司炉工”，指人人都等却无人说出名字的那样人而不是那位消防员，是事情里人人都等、却无人说出名字的人。
fireman 意为“消防员”，指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一位，到 1970 年这一位成了计划里的一行。
fireman 意为“消防员”，队长二月写道，整件事的称谢之事是一座消防站和三个夜晚的说出名字。
fireman 意为“消防员”，我记得的是计划里被说出名字的那一位，1972 年结束了，至今仍被说成消防站里最安静的一位。
fireman 为抽象总称，母亲 1974 年说，一位消防员是唯一会因为被好好说出名字而变得更好的人。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1963 年队长感谢了一位消防站里没有一位长官肯说出名字的消防员，他说道谢才是那个夜晚的全部。（thank a fireman）
那位消防员，指的是那一位本身而不是消防车，经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被说出名字。（fireman）
那座消防站里每一位消防员旁边都有同一顶矮矮的头盔。（fireman）
最远那道门边那位消防员，指的是他们留给孩子们的那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（fireman）
叔叔说那位司炉工就是那件事的全部，指的是那样人而不是那位消防员。（fireman）
1974 年母亲说，一位消防员是唯一会因为被好好说出名字而变得更好的人。（fireman）
answers: In 1963 the captain thanked a fireman that no officer in the station would have named, and he said the thanking was the whole of the night.
The fireman, meaning the man himself and not the engine, ran three nights and stayed unnamed in the book.
Every fireman in that station had the same short helmet beside him.
The fireman at the far door, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the fireman was the whole of the matter, meaning the stoker and not the man.
A fireman, my mother said in 1974, is the only one that improves by being named.
